---
title: "Learn Jammi by running it"
---

Jammi is an embeddable AI engine: register data sources and query them with SQL,
generate embeddings and search them, run and fine-tune models, and measure the
results — in your own process, or against a server, through one API. This book
teaches every one of those capabilities with a program you run. Each chapter is
code and the prose that explains it; nothing is a screenshot of a result.

## How to read it

Every chapter has an **Open in Colab** badge under its title. A notebook's first
cell installs this release of Jammi — the CUDA engine on a GPU runtime, the CPU
engine otherwise — and the cookbook's fixtures, then every cell runs top to
bottom. To run a chapter locally instead:

```bash
pip install "jammi-ai[embedded]" "jammi-cookbook @ git+https://github.com/f-inverse/jammi-ai#subdirectory=cookbook/book"
```

Every chapter runs real, pretrained models from the Hugging Face Hub, downloaded
on first use. Chapters run at the `small` scale by default: small samples of the
datasets and a compact text encoder. Most chapters take seconds to minutes on a
CPU; the ones that fine-tune an encoder take from a quarter of an hour to a few
hours on a CPU, and minutes on a GPU. Setting `JAMMI_COOKBOOK_SCALE=full` runs the
same code over the published datasets and a larger text encoder, on a GPU.

## The path

Start with the quickstart; after it, each part stands on its own. A part's short
recipes walk a capability's verbs one step at a time; its chapters take a
capability deep and measure it.

| Part | What you learn |
|---|---|
| **Start here** | Install, connect, register a source, embed it and search it; the two datasets the longer chapters use. |
| **Search** | Dense, lexical and fused retrieval; image, audio and cross-modal search; how much recall the ANN index gives up; how the index grows by segments; storing vectors at lower precision; auditing every search. |
| **Models and inference** | The model catalog; models served at an endpoint; the dtype inference runs at; quantized checkpoints; how a model stage behaves at any parallelism. |
| **Evaluation** | Retrieval, classification and NER quality; evaluation and provenance channels; the error each failure raises; calibration of predicted uncertainty. |
| **Fine-tuning** | LoRA fine-tuning; choosing a method; regression heads; image and audio encoders; what acceleration a job got; one job trained across many ranks. |
| **Graphs and prediction** | Neighbour graphs, propagation and lineage; predicting from retrieved context. |
| **Data that changes** | Mutable tables; a feature store; change-data-capture topics; point-in-time joins; detecting and repairing stale results; editing an embedding table in place; storage that ends with the session. |
| **Where data lives** | Object storage; Postgres and MySQL as sources in one query. |
| **Running Jammi** | One program embedded or remote; Flight SQL; compound queries; the CLI, Rust and TypeScript; jobs; multi-tenancy; a production catalog and broker; backup, health, metrics and traces. |
| **Case study: graph machine learning** | Everything together on ogbn-arxiv: build a graph, propagate over it, fine-tune on it, predict with calibrated coverage — and the theory each step implements. |

## How it stays honest

Every chapter shows the numbers it just measured and checks the claims it teaches
against them: an ordering, a bound or an equality the engine guarantees, so a claim
holds on your machine as it does on ours, and a chapter whose claim fails stops
and names it. Every chapter runs on every change to the engine it documents, and
every notebook is also run nightly exactly as a reader runs it — installed from
PyPI in a fresh runtime. The [API reference](chapters/api-reference.qmd) lists every
verb the book calls.
